title: pgwarc_lance quality query attempt identity envelope (prospective v1, synthetic)
description: Prospective, synthetic envelope for correlating a future quality query attempt. This schema checks structural consistency only. A structurally valid envelope is not evidence that any PostgreSQL backend existed or still exists, that a statement or transaction was actually executed or identified, that cancellation was requested or completed, that a rollback happened, or that session/transaction resources were cleaned up. attempt_id is a correlation-only handle and carries no authenticity, ordering, or ownership guarantee. session_identity is an author-supplied claim, not a value observed from PostgreSQL in this repository. transaction_identity is fixed to the single unobserved state for v1 and never asserts a transaction id, rollback, or cleanup. No cancellation, termination, retry, or rollback fields are defined; unsupported claims are rejected by additionalProperties=false. This contract is not produced, consumed, or enforced by eval-quality, doctor_run_directory, run finalization, or make verify.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Only v1 is defined, as a strict JSON integer.

attempt_id.description: Correlation-only non-empty identifier for one synthetic attempt. It is not an authentic backend, statement, or transaction identifier.

capture_state.description: Whether the synthetic envelope claims a captured session identity or records it as unavailable.

session_identity.description: Null when capture_state is 'unavailable'. When capture_state is 'captured' it is exactly the two-field author-supplied claim {backend_pid, backend_start}; it is not independently verified against PostgreSQL.

backend_pid.description: Claimed positive backend process id. Booleans are not integers and are rejected.

backend_start.description: ISO-8601 date-time with an explicit timezone offset. A date-time without a timezone is rejected.

transaction_identity.description: Exactly {state: 'unobserved'} for v1. No transaction id, rollback, or cleanup claim is allowed.

capture_source.description: 'none' when capture_state is 'unavailable'. 'query_session' when capture_state is 'captured'. The source names where a future runtime would capture identity; it does not prove a capture happened.
